constraints: All products fit in a 32-bit integer.

examples.explain: Only the position holding the 0 gets a non-zero product.

hints: answer[i] splits into two independent parts: the product of everything to the left of i, and everything to the right.
Build a prefix-product array and a suffix-product array. Each answer is one multiplication.
Write the prefix products straight into the output, then sweep from the right with a single running suffix.

insight.mnemonic: Left pass fills, right pass finishes.
insight.oneLiner: Everything-except-i = (everything left of i) × (everything right of i). Two sweeps with running products.

recall.a: It's banned, and it fails on zeros (division by zero, or one zero making every product 0).
The output array stores the prefix products; the suffix is a single running variable.
recall.q: How does the optimal solution reach O(1) extra space?

signals: answer depends on everything left and right
insight.why: Each running product is reused for the next index instead of being recomputed, so both sweeps are O(n). No division means zeros can't break it.

oneLiner: Everything-except-i = (everything left of i) × (everything right of i). Two sweeps with running products.

pitfalls.explain: Dividing the total product by nums[i] fails when nums contains a 0 (and it's not allowed here).
pitfalls.title: Division breaks on zeros

pitfalls.explain: Write res[i] = prefix *before* multiplying nums[i] into prefix.
pitfalls.title: Included nums[i] in its own product

solutions.idea: For each i, multiply all other elements. Correct, but it redoes nearly the same work n times.
solutions.name: Multiply everything else

solutions.idea: Precompute products to the left and right of every index, then multiply pairwise.
solutions.name: Prefix and suffix arrays

footnotes.text: The output array doubles as the prefix table, so the only extra memory is two integers - O(1) beyond the answer.

solutions.idea: Store left products in the output, then multiply in right products with a running variable.

class Solution:
    def productExceptSelf(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` is the **product of every element except `nums[i]`**.

Solve it in O(n) time **without using division**. Every such product fits in a 32-bit integer.
title: Product of Array Except Self
